generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, succeeding on your own terms runs across your whole degree, not just the final exam. You direct a research project or a placement, notice the analytical skill and professional networks it builds, and keep asking what success in psychology means to you. Those small rounds let you say, with evidence, what you have become.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two psychology finalists reach the same point with similar marks. One banks the grade and waits for graduation. The other directs her dissertation, notices the research skills and placement networks she has built, and keeps defining what success means to her. By graduation she can describe, with evidence, the psychologist she has become, and the first student cannot.
generatedProse.summary: In psychology, succeeding works best as one practice you own. You run all three strands together across the degree: direct your study, build your capital, and define and articulate your success as a psychologist. It is the practice, not any single mark, that shows what you have become.

check.body: A final-year student directs her own revision, notices the resilience and networks she has built, and can say with evidence what she set out to achieve. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next report, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next report improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That she is succeeding as one practice: the engine, her graduate capital and her own definition of success are working together.
_items.feedback: Yes. All three strands are running at once, which is what succeeding on your own terms looks like.

_items.text: That she has a high final grade and nothing more needs saying.
_items.feedback: A grade alone is not the point. She is drawing on all three strands, not just her marks.

_items.text: That she has finished the engine strand and can now drop it.
_items.feedback: Directing your own learning does not stop. The engine keeps running as you become a graduate.

_items.text: That graduate capital is the only strand that matters in the end.
_items.feedback: Capital is one strand. Here it works alongside the engine and her own definition of success.
